problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 0 \\ -3 & \text{i}\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following elementary row operations: 

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{3}{1+\text{i}}{R}_{1}
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations to a Complex Matrix
examples.problem:
Given the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14045065/assets/766ddf98a05c69ef0791858a7f32457425cf1a9650d2205227ffc7d9d173d2e7.png) find the result of applying to $A$ the following elementary row operations:

$$
R_1 := \dfrac{1}{\textrm{i}}R_1, \qquad R_2 := R_2 - 2\textrm{i}R_1
$$
examples.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}\text{i} & -\text{i} \\ 2+2\text{i} & 1\end{aligned}]\, &  & {R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2+2\text{i} & 1\end{aligned}]\, &  & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2\text{i}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1+2\text{i}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14045065/assets/9fef320d53c15c2820719bb1d0dfabb00afa6200b43279e3137fbb25c4e67e2d.png)

feedback.worked_solution:
Multiplying the matrix by the vector using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & 2-\text{i} & 3-\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i} & 1+2\text{i} & 1+3\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\text{i} \\ -\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(1-\text{i})(\text{i})+(2-\text{i})(-\text{i})+(3-\text{i})(1+\text{i}) \\ (1+\text{i})(\text{i})+(1+2\text{i})(-\text{i})+(1+3\text{i})(1+\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(1+\text{i})+(-1-2\text{i})+(4+2\text{i}) \\ (-1+\text{i})+(2-\text{i})+(-2+4\text{i})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4+\text{i} \\ -1+4\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
